Some homepage event and chart enum values remain source-defined rather than guessed.

novel_features.name: Entitlement-aware scorecards
novel_features.description: Show Tickertape score dimensions, locked fields, entry-point signals, and red flags without silently dropping premium data.
novel_features.rationale: The scorecard envelope carries source-specific lock and element metadata that generic quote clients discard.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Choose this when an agent needs transparent Tickertape opinion data and must distinguish locked from absent fields.

novel_features.name: Company publication timeline
novel_features.description: Combine live company events, news, results, and investor-presentation metadata into a dated source-labelled stream.
novel_features.rationale: The CLI can compose several Tickertape summary arrays into one agent-sized view without inventing cross-source equivalence.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Choose this for a current company-history pass before drilling into individual reports.

novel_features.name: Live multi-asset lookup
novel_features.description: Triages Indian stocks, mutual funds, ETFs, indices, and US securities through one live command while retaining source-specific identity fields.
novel_features.rationale: Tickertape exposes an unusually broad cross-asset research graph, and the CLI can route it without creating a local mirror.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Choose this when the asset class is unknown or an agent needs consistent first-pass research.

novel_features.name: Access and provenance envelope
novel_features.description: Explain source host, route, observation time, entity identity, lock state, and entitlement errors for any live result.
novel_features.rationale: Undocumented web-app routes and premium fields make silent omission dangerous; the CLI can preserve the evidence envelope on every call.
novel_features.example: tickertape-pp-cli inspect access company scorecard RELI --agent
novel_features.why_it_matters: Choose this when an agent must explain whether a result is public, locked, authenticated, or unavailable.

novel_features.name: MMI component brief
novel_features.description: Turn the live Market Mood Index payload into a concise timestamped brief of fear/greed, FII, momentum, volatility, and component signals.
novel_features.rationale: The MMI endpoint returns heterogeneous indicators that benefit from a stable agent-facing presentation without persisting a snapshot.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Choose this for current market context, not as a trading signal or historical series.

novel_features.name: Source-specific company research brief
novel_features.description: Compose live company identity, summary, scorecard, reports, and access state into one bounded triage response.
novel_features.rationale: The CLI can join related Tickertape routes for one request without storing domain history or flattening source-specific opinions.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Choose this for the first pass on a company when raw endpoint-by-endpoint calls would waste agent context.

novel_features.name: Live screener catalog navigator
novel_features.description: Organize equity and mutual-fund filters, categories, universes, and prebuilt screens while preserving premium markers.
novel_features.rationale: The catalog is public metadata, while saved screens and query execution are separate sensitive or contract-uncertain workflows.

narrative.headline: Live, provenance-aware Tickertape research without stale local market data
narrative.value_prop: Use Tickertape's public Indian and US research surfaces from the terminal: company fundamentals, scorecards, mutual funds, screen metadata, MMI, deal ideas, and US assets. Every domain-data call is live and carries source and access context; locked or entitlement-aware fields are surfaced rather than silently omitted.
narrative.auth_narrative: Public research commands require no credential. The current EgoBrowser profile demonstrated authenticated page traffic for user, credit, portfolio, ratings, forecast, AI summary, and deal routes; when a supported secure credential/session mechanism is wired for optional entitlement-aware calls, credentials may live only in the secure auth store or permissioned auth config. Never copy credentials, cookies, headers, or personal portfolio values into output or domain-data storage.

quickstart.comment: Verify the live-read configuration without making a domain-data request.
Start with current market mood and component indicators.
Inspect score dimensions while preserving locked fields.
Read a mutual-fund summary once an ID is known.
Use the same CLI for a US asset overview.

troubleshoots.symptom: A response is 401, 403, or contains locked fields
troubleshoots.fix: Treat it as access metadata; configure only the approved secure auth mechanism and never copy cookies or tokens into command arguments or files.
Use screen filters, prebuilt, or universes first; query bodies and premium-field behavior are intentionally not guessed.

troubleshoots.symptom: A chart or event query rejects a duration/type value
troubleshoots.fix: Use the values exposed by the live metadata/page contract and preserve the upstream error instead of retrying guessed enums.

troubleshoots.symptom: A route is slow or rate-limited
troubleshoots.fix: Retry conservatively with backoff and rerun the live command; the CLI does not serve cached domain data.

narrative.when_to_use: Use Tickertape for live, read-only investment research across Indian stocks, mutual funds, ETFs, indices, and US securities. Reach for it when scorecards, red flags, entry-point signals, MMI, deal ideas, or provenance-aware access state matter. Use a broker tool for orders and authoritative holdings, and a fundamentals source for deeper source-linked operating history.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI for orders, trades, broker linking, fills, taxes, or authoritative executed holdings.
Do not use it for watchlists, saved screens, portfolio mutations, social actions, exports, payments, loans, gold, or account opening.
Do not treat Tickertape scorecards or MMI as a universal investment recommendation or as a cross-source consensus.
